actions: Retried public resolution of Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.16441066 and exact-title/DOI searches for non-author reproduction or failure evidence. The peer-reviewed article continues to state that all simulation/analysis code is at that Zenodo DOI, but current public search transport still did not expose the record file list/checksums, and no clear independent rerun was established.

Recovered the version-of-record random-interpolation protocol from Communications Biology: for each adjacent frame pair, flatten and concatenate the pair, randomly shuffle to destroy spatial locality while preserving pixel-intensity statistics, reshape, and insert stochastic content between the pair. Frame dropout removes a fixed proportion of frames; the paper reports robustness under up to 50% frame dropout.

Built a stricter source-derived recurrence-specific control on binary moving-bar videos using identical sequence-level translation-normalized input and nearly parameter-matched recurrent versus non-recurrent models. The recurrent model was a leaky ReLU recurrent network with per-step layer normalization (14,284 parameters); the non-recurrent control was a framewise MLP with the same per-frame input and time-averaged readout (14,322 parameters).

Used 12 direction classes, 14 frames, 12x12 binary videos, sparse Bernoulli pixel noise p=0.01, 1,500 clean training clips and 500 test clips per seed, three independent training seeds, and 10 epochs. This remains source-derived, not an exact reproduction of the paper's 512-neuron/T=100 architecture or DVS/RGB tasks.

Implemented inserted-frame corruption as a source-like approximation: for each selected adjacent gap, concatenate the two 12x12 frames, randomly permute all 288 values, take one frame-sized 144-value slice after shuffling, reshape, and insert it. Swept the fraction of corrupted gaps (0.25, 0.5, 1.0) and inserted noise-block length g (1, 2, 4). The all-gap g=1 condition is the closest tested analogue to the article text, but exact code semantics remain unresolved until the Zenodo artifact is accessible.
Measured hidden-state recovery after a single mid-sequence insertion block by aligning the recurrent hidden trajectory to the clean trajectory over the next seven clean frames.

public_sources.title: Representation Transfer via Invariant Input-driven Continuous Attractors for Fast Domain Adaptation
source_facts: 512-neuron vanilla RNN modules; leaky recurrent ReLU dynamics with tau=2 and per-step layer normalization; Direction pretraining uses T=100 moving-bar clips over 12 directions and sparse Bernoulli noise p=0.01.
Random interpolation inserts shuffled content between adjacent frames after flattening/concatenating the pair so spatial locality is destroyed while pixel-intensity statistics are preserved.

The article attributes temporal-perturbation robustness to coherent recurrent dynamics and reports near-perfect Direction decoding plus robustness to frame dropout/interpolation on real gesture inputs.

design.translation_normalization: sequence-level shift using first-frame active-pixel centroid; both models receive identical normalized frames

source_derived_ablation.interpretation: The trained recurrent state does contract back toward the clean trajectory after a localized corruption, but in this simplified primitive-isolated task that recovery is too slow to confer robustness to repeated inserted-frame corruption. The non-recurrent matched control retained substantially more of its clean accuracy at every tested corruption level, including the closest all-gap/g=1 analogue. This further weakens a generic claim that recurrence alone explains the paper's interpolation robustness and narrows the remaining hypothesis to attractor-specific training/geometry or details of the actual source architecture and data.
scope: Not an exact reproduction: 14-frame 12x12 synthetic videos and smaller recurrent state replace the paper's T=100, 512-neuron pretrained Direction module and real DVS/RGB transfer pipeline.
The inserted-frame generator is a source-text approximation because the Zenodo implementation remains inaccessible; exact reshape/splitting semantics may differ.

The non-recurrent framewise model has access to the same translation-normalized frames and can exploit absolute displacement from the normalized origin without recurrent memory; this is intentional for testing whether primitive isolation alone is sufficient in this simplified regime.
Clean accuracy differs between models, so both absolute accuracy and clean-normalized retention are reported. The robustness conclusion is limited to these matched synthetic conditions.

Hidden-state recovery is measured against the model's own clean trajectory, not against a learned manifold ridge; it is a contraction/recovery diagnostic, not a direct reproduction of the paper's manifold-angle analysis.

evidence_added_this_run: Under the closest source-like all-gap/g=1 inserted interpolation, the leaky LayerNorm RNN fell from 54.67% clean to 22.47% while the nearly parameter-matched non-recurrent control stayed at 63.13% from 65.73% clean; clean-normalized retention was 41.3% vs 96.1%.

The recurrent hidden state did recover toward its clean trajectory after a single corruption block, but only gradually: g=1 RMS distance fell 0.2609->0.1734 over seven clean frames; g=4 fell 0.8079->0.5712.
Across all corruption fractions/block lengths, the non-recurrent control was more robust in this simplified primitive-isolated setting.
candidate_update.interpretation: Two successive source-derived controls now indicate that explicit low-dimensional primitive isolation is sufficient for substantial robustness without a generic recurrence advantage, and the source-like inserted-frame test removes the previous small recurrent edge seen under a fixed-length interpolation analogue. The scientifically useful remaining question is not 'recurrence versus no recurrence' but whether the paper's attractor-specific pretraining geometry and manifold contraction produce robustness that a matched feedforward primitive encoder cannot reproduce.

exact_next_action: Continue public metadata/file-list resolution for Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.16441066 and exact-title/citation searches for a non-author rerun. If artifact access remains blocked, move from generic recurrence to an attractor-specific causal test: train a paper-like leaky ReLU + per-step LayerNorm direction network on longer T=100 moving-bar sequences, quantify manifold participation ratio/flow alignment and perturbation contraction, then compare its source-like inserted-interpolation robustness against (a) a parameter-matched feedforward primitive encoder and (b) a recurrent control trained to the same direction accuracy without an explicit low-dimensional manifold objective/geometry. The key decision is whether robustness tracks attractor geometry/contraction after matching clean accuracy, not recurrence itself.
